title: Ukraine and FBI uncover ransomware network tied to $40.5 million in payments; four in custody
date_note: Announced by Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office on November 18; the activity was documented over about two years.
org: Office of the Prosecutor General of Ukraine / FBI
geo_basis: agency location (searches in Kyiv and 11 regions)
actor: Unnamed ransomware network (Ukrainian prosecutors say it includes former Conti members)
summary: Ukrainian prosecutors, working with the FBI, ran 66 searches in Kyiv and 11 regions and served four suspected key members with notice of suspicion; all four are in custody. Prosecutors say at least 28 companies paid more than $40.5 million and that the core group of 27 sits within a network of over 60 people in eight jurisdictions. Attackers posed as IT support to obtain credentials and install remote-access software.
plain: Police in Ukraine and the FBI raided a ransomware gang that tricked staff by pretending to be IT support. Four suspects are in custody and victims paid over $40 million.
exec: Shows fake help-desk calls leading to remote-access tools and ransomware at large firms; a reminder to verify any unsolicited IT support contact.
action: Train staff to verify unsolicited IT support calls through a known channel, and restrict installation of remote-access software to approved tools.
impact: At least 28 companies paid more than $40.5 million; one US company lost 1.4 TB of data and paid $5 million after a $10 million demand.

validation.note: Hromadske and UNN, read in full, both report the Prosecutor General's Office announcement; the original announcement was not read. Ransomware strain not named in either; the Conti link is the prosecutors' statement. Suspects presumed innocent.
